mapper.verbatim_quote: ຕ້ອງເກັບຮັກສາໄວ້ຢ່າງຫນ້ອຍ ສິບ (1 0) ປີ
mapper.rationale: Explicit minimum retention period of at least 10 years for documents/data/electronic copies satisfies the 7.3 minimum-retention scoring branch.

verifier.reason: Article 16 mandates retention of documents, data and electronic copies for a minimum of 10 years ("ຕ້ອງເກັບຮັກສາໄວ້ຢ່າງຫນ້ອຍ ສິບ (10) ປີ"). This specifies a minimum duration explicitly. Although the context is commercial banking product services, the retention requirement is quantified and enforceable. Under 7.3 scoring tree, this meets the condition: "A requirement exists to retain data for at least a specified minimum period (duration in days/months/years explicitly stated...)." Score 1 applies.

mapper.verbatim_quote: ໃນການຄູ້ມຄອງວຽກງານຄວາມປອດໄພໄຊເບີ ກະຊວງເຕັກໂນໂລຊີ ແລະ ການສີສານ ມີ ສິດ ແລະ ຫາທີ່
mapper.rationale: Evidence of a dedicated, horizontal cybersecurity legal framework (Law on Cybersecurity) with a designated ministry managing it economy-wide; framework EXISTS so 7.2 (lack of framework) scores 0 per inverted polarity.

verifier.reason: Art. 88 of the Cybersecurity Law (ກົດໝາຍວ່າດ້ວຍ ຄວາມປອດໄພໄຊເບີ) enumerates the rights and duties of the Ministry of Technology and Communications in cybersecurity work. The provision itself does not establish the cybersecurity legal framework; rather, it allocates institutional responsibilities and powers. Economy-level indicator 7.2 asks whether a DEDICATED cybersecurity legal framework exists. The presence of Art. 88 establishing ministerial roles and duties is evidence that a dedicated cybersecurity law exists in Laos. Per 7.2 scoring tree: if a dedicated cybersecurity legal framework applies across all sectors (horizontal) → score 0. This law, as referenced by its title and scope, appears to be a horizontal cybersecurity act. Trap checks: (1) Not economy-level discovery restatement (Art. 88 alone does not constitute a separate discovery if the law's existence is already recorded at economy level); (2) The provision itself shows cybersecurity-specific governance structure, confirming the framework is dedicated, not non-dedicated. Score branch: ELSE → 0 (a dedicated cybersecurity legal framework exists).

mapper.verbatim_quote: ຕ້ອງສ້າງຕັ້ງສະຖານີດາວທຽມພາກພື້ນດິນ ຢູ່ໃນ ສປປ ລາວ ເພືອຮັບ-ສົ່ງສັນຍານອິນເຕີເນັດ ລະຫວ່າງ
mapper.rationale: Mandate to establish local ground satellite station as precondition to provide satellite-based internet service = infrastructure requirement, not mere licensing/storage.

verifier.reason: Item 20 of Art. 13 mandates: "ຕ້ອງສ້າງຕັ້ງສະຖານີດາວທຽມພາກພື້ນດິນ ຢູ່ໃນ ສປປ ລາວ" (must establish/set up a satellite ground station within Laos) as a condition for providing internet service business operations, specifically to send/receive internet signals between countries. This is a primary barrier to data movement: an explicit establishment mandate for dedicated local physical infrastructure (a satellite ground station) as a precondition to provide certain services using data. This satisfies 6.3's definition and scoring tree branch: "There is at least one infrastructure requirement acting as a barrier/precondition to data movement or service supply" → score 1. The trap checks do not apply: this is not a licensing/registration scheme (it is not 9.4), not a security control on existing infrastructure, and not a general operational requirement on already-established facilities—it is a build/establish mandate.

mapper.verbatim_quote: ໄດ້ຮັບອະນຸຍາດຈາກເຈົ້າຂອງຂໍມູນ ແລະ ຮັບປະກັນວ່າຜູ້ຮັບ ສາມາດປົກປ້ອງຂໍມູນ ນັ້ນໄດ້
mapper.rationale: Cross-border transfer of data, including personal data, is conditioned on data owner's consent and recipient's capacity to protect data — a consent-based conditional flow regime covering personal data, applies horizontally to all persons/entities, scores 1 per Guide p.54.

verifier.reason: Article 17 requires consent from the data owner and recipient guarantees for data transfer/transmission, but this is not a conditional flow regime under 6.4. The provision mandates CONDITIONS (consent + security encryption for sensitive data + integrity assurance + contractual compliance + cessation on non-compliance) for lawful transfer. However, 6.4 specifically applies to conditions that PERMIT transfer to destinations whose data protection is adequate/equivalent, or are justified by other safeguards (consent, adequacy self-assessment, contracts, government approval). Article 17 does not establish a framework permitting cross-border transfer conditioned on destination adequacy or equivalent protection—it simply sets general data-handling requirements for transmission. The trap check: "Must not transfer UNLESS [condition]" is 6.4; Article 17 imposes operational/safety conditions on transfer itself, not a conditional CROSS-BORDER transfer regime gating outbound flows to adequate jurisdictions. No evidence of border-crossing conditionality.

escalation.reason: Art. 17 permits cross-border transfer of personal data (and official data) out of Laos ONLY IF the data owner's consent is obtained and it does not conflict with law — a default-prohibition-plus-condition (consent) pattern. That is a conditional flow regime (6.4), not a per-se ban (6.1 trap avoided: a compliant transfer path exists via consent). Covers personal data, so branch 1 → score 1. (Official/government data portion not scored.)

ຈໍາເປັນຜ່ານຂັ້ນຕອນການດໍາເນີນຄະດີອາຍາ ຫຼື ມີຄໍາຕັດສິນຂອງສານ ແລະ ບໍ່ຈໍາເປັນມີການກະທໍາຜິດເກີດຂຶ້ນ
mapper.rationale: Ministry can designate persons/entities on a terrorism list based on its own evidentiary assessment, explicitly bypassing court order/judicial decision - non-judicial government access/action on personal data of listed persons.

verifier.reason: Art. 18 permits the Ministry of Public Security to add persons/entities to a domestic blacklist and request international action WITHOUT requiring a prior court order or independent judicial authorization. The provision states the Ministry may designate individuals based on "substantial and sufficient evidence" of counter-terrorism/financing activities, and may forward requests to foreign states "immediately through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs without need for criminal proceedings or court judgment." This is discretionary authority by a non-judicial body (Ministry of Public Security) to access/designate individuals based on government assessment alone, triggering 7.5 score 1 branch: "Government access to personal data without independent judicial authorization."
